title: A writer who stages a killing where religious and political authority already share the space turns it from a hidden execution into the community's public spectacle
body:
- Staging the death at a gathering that holds evangelical leaders, conservative politicians, and paramilitary groups fuses sacred, political, and armed authority into one symbolic space.
- The protagonist walks in on their own, which lets the killing read as chosen martyrdom rather than an imposed punishment.
- A religious leader publicly names the visitor to the crowd, so private recognition becomes a shared act by everyone present.
- Because religious and political authority already sit in the same event, the crowd can carry the killing out openly as a community ritual instead of concealing it as an execution.
conversion: A killing staged where sacred and political authority converge becomes the community's public ritual rather than a hidden execution
